description.narrative: Core support to Global Partnership for the Prevention of Armed Conflict

Kärnstöd till Global Partnership for the Prevention of Armed Conflict (GPPAC) - ett globalt nätverk som sammanlänkar civilsamhälle med relevanta lokala, nationella, regionala och internationella aktörer och institutioner för att gemensamt bidra till att skifta fokus från ett reaktivt till ett proaktivt och förebyggande förhållningssätt till väpnat våld och väpnad konflikt. GPPAC består av femton regionala nätverk med medlemmar i över sextio länder. Den Strategiska Planens tre komponenter speglar organisationens förändringsteori och är: Enabling collaboration, Improving practice och Influencing policy - Möjliggöra samarbete, Förbättra praxis och Påverka policy.

The vision of the Global Partnership for the Prevention of Armed Conflict (GPPAC) is to seek a world where violence and armed conflicts are prevented and resolved by peaceful means, based on justice, gender equity, sustainable development, and human security for all. GPPAC aims to contribute to the shift from reaction to prevention when dealing with violence and armed conflict by linking civil society with local, national, regional and international actors and institutions. The objectives and expected results in the new Strategic Plan for the period 2021-2025 are: 1. To further the implementation of peacebuilding, achieving change and sustaining peace at the local level. 2. To include the needs, perspectives and expertise of local peacebuilders from diverse societal backgrounds in the analysis, design, solutions and monitoring of peacebuilding and conflict prevention processes at all levels, with a specific focus on the agency of women and young peacebuilders. 3. For every relevant stakeholder to apply a conflict-sensitive and peacebuilding lens to the design and delivery of their climate security and emerging threats policies and practice.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
Sida has been providing core support to GPPAC for the period 2017-2019 (23 MSEK) and decided to extend the support with an additional 10 MSEK in 2020. The main reason was to align with the new GPPAC Strategic Plan from 2021 in a possible renewed support. The main funder besides Sida for this period was the Netherlands, which provided support to the Prevention Up Front (PUF) programme, as implemented by GPPAC and its partners. The Sida core support complemented the Dutch support and was directed towards two of the objectives in the PUF programme (as selected by GPPAC). In June 2020, GPPAC informed Sida that the Dutch MFA would no longer be funding GPPAC from 2021 as it had decided to allow funding to a decreased number of organisations for its new round of 5 year support to international CSOs. As a result, Sida decided to support GPPAC with an additional 5 MSEK until 30 June 2021 to allow GPPAC to put in place a transition plan in support of necessary changes to the organisation. The current support to GPPAC follows the period 1 July 2021-2023 (please see PLANit 13097).
As for all Sida partners, the implementation during this period was shadowed by the Covid-19 pandemic, which forced GPPAC to re-think plans and move the network online. GPPAC has noted that positive aspects include that the network was able to meet in greater numbers and more frequent in the virtual space and that the online world opened new doors in engagement with policymakers. However, on the downside, members who work in the most remote areas or are active in conflict zones often lack a stable internet connection and suffer from frequent power cuts.
Examples of results achieved GPPAC is the largest network of peacebuilding organisations with more than 250 members and activities in all regions of the world. A key part of GPPAC's work as a network is to open up space for meaningful exchanges between local peacebuilders and decision makers at all levels to advance more locally-informed decision-making on matters of peacebuilding and conflict prevention. As Sida provides core support to the organisation there are a wide range of results reported. The following highlight results on a global level and that illustrate key links between local peacebuilding and normative policy work primarily taking place in capitals.
The UN Peacebuilding Architecture Review (UNPBAR) Together with the local peacebuilders who make up the network, GPPAC in various ways brought the perspectives of local peacebuilders into the discussions around the UNPBAR process in 2020. GPPAC reports that it recognises its contribution as the joint Security Council resolution 2558 states that local peacebuilders are critical stakeholders and calls for a more coordinated and inclusive regional peacebuilding architecture. Furthermore, the 2020 Secretary General Report specifically highlights the GPPAC-FTI participatory video methodology project in Kyrgyzstan as an approach to youth empowerment towards playing key roles in identifying peacebuilding needs and to take them up with local authorities (para. 21). Also, the advocacy capacity training of members, GPPAC policy support and publications and the engagement itself provided an opportunity for local peacebuilders to better understand regional and global peacebuilding space and decide for themselves how to use the space.
The UN Community Engagement Guidelines (UN-CEG) In 2016, the UN General Assembly and the UN Security Council expressed their commitment to building and sustaining peace and called for strategic and operational partnerships, including with civil society actors. As a result, a joint UN-Civil Society Working Group was set up that included GPPAC, Quaker United Nations Office (QUNO) and the International Peace Institute (IPI). The aim of the Working Group was to facilitate a truly participatory process to develop the UN system-wide Community Engagement Guidelines (UNCEG) on Peacebuilding and Sustaining Peace. As part of the Working Group, GPPAC ensured that the voices of local peacebuilders were included across all steps of the process. In August 2020, the United Nations Community Engagement Guidelines on Peacebuilding and Sustaining Peace were published, reflecting the needs and perspectives of civil society in a participatory and consultative process. Building on this, GPPAC together with the Global Network of Women Peacebuilders (GNWP) developed a practical resource and training for local peacebuilders to help build stronger partnerships with the UN.
The Civil Society-UN Prevention Platform The Civil Society-UN Prevention Platform is co-facilitated by QUNO and GPPAC in conjunction with the UNDPPA and a coordinating group of cross-sectoral expertise. In 2020, the CS-UN Prevention Platform facilitated a series of 5 inclusive and cross-sectoral discussions titled UN Prevention Across Sectors and Institutions: Pathways for Effective Prevention. In these discussions, local peacebuilders and other global, regional and national stakeholders came together to reflect and mobilize action on climate change, mediation, gender analysis and Youth, Peace and Security. The CS-UN Prevention Platform is important because it fosters engagement with Peace and Development Advisors (PDAs) and civil society and thus allows GPPAC members to advance their perspective on prevention, integrate their methodologies for action and maintain multi stakeholder space for dialogue and collaboration on prevention.
